verdicts.method: OccSplit: train as plain full fine-tuning, keep the part of the update that lands on the old skills' occupied subspace private
verdicts.verdict: PLAUSIBLE, CONDITIONAL. Most likely to pass its Step 0 and the safest of the three, because training is literally full FT: speed equals FT (t90 1.43-1.64M). But layer-1 occupancy must be standardised and k chosen by a function check; the worst-state eps as specified overshoots the parameter budget. Offline on 5 full-FT checkpoints, held-out Pick states: (1) Standardised layer 1 at 99% average energy: k = 23/21/18, private 18.7k = 12.9% of the actor. The old skill's shared view changes by drift 0.10-0.24 and clipped arm action 0.008-0.013, against FT's 9.8-17.9 and 0.084-0.128. (2) Worst-state eps = 1e-2: k = 32/29/67 (24.6%); changes <= 0.005 and <= 0.0008. (3) The 23:55 post-hoc GPM-removal failure (Pick 0.81-0.90) comes from raw layer-1 energy (k1 = 10): drift 2.2-3.3, arm change 0.037-0.049. Small-magnitude relative-position inputs drop out of a raw-energy basis. So that failure was the layer-1 metric, not the idea. (4) Among all measured networks, the smallest arm change that fell below 0.95 on Pick was 0.0245; std-avg99 sits 2-3x below that and eps = 1e-2 about 30x below. (5) The worst-state criterion is costly and does not generalise: eps = 1e-3 gives k = 33/40/159 (43% of the actor), 1e-4 gives 33/98/224 (65%, over the 30% KILL bar), and at the chosen k the held-out worst residual is 10-15x eps. (6) The free part merged into the shared trunk is only 5-14% of the FT update's norm^2 at eps <= 1e-2, and 31% at std-avg99.
verdicts.closest_prior: Input-subspace methods make the same split but discard the occupied part: GPM (Saha 2021), Adam-NSCL (Wang 2021), InfLoRA (Liang & Li 2024), NESS (Pham et al. 2026, a LoRA-style update confined to the input null space), NuSA-CL (2025), and AlphaEdit for edits. Task-vector masking and merging keep a per-task part and drop or rescale the rest: TALL-masks, Localize-and-Stitch, EMR-Merging. Parameter isolation in RL: PackNet (best in Continual World) and PNN. Not seen elsewhere: keeping the occupied part as a private out x k map while merging the free part into the shared weights, so the new skill stays exact and old skills see the free part only through their residual.
verdicts.risks: (1) Proxies predict sim retention only moderately (Spearman -0.53 to -0.82), and two RL networks with similar proxies differed by 14 points (block09 0.98 vs block095 0.84), so Step 0 must be a sim eval. The std-avg99 point (12.9%, inside the <= 15% GO budget) is the one at risk. eps = 1e-2 is very likely safe but at 24.6% breaks that budget. (2) The parameter story is close to cheap alternatives: 13-25% per skill is near LoRA r=16 (16%) and SVD-truncated FT deltas. OccSplit must win on speed (FT speed vs LoRA's unmeasured speed) and on exactness, not on size. (3) 'Share the free capacity' is largely cosmetic: the free part is 5-31% of the update's norm^2 and no old skill reads it, so a reviewer will call it a subspace-masked task vector. (4) Chains: union occupancy grows, so free share shrinks and private size per skill grows; evidence from one skill will not convince. (5) a2r: a pre-norm LayerNorm + SiLU residual stream with 512-d inputs is likely much less concentrated than 256-unit tanh layers, and PointNet's per-point Linears need per-point occupancy, so the private part may exceed 30% there. (6) It covers the trunk only; heads, log-std and critics are per skill anyway.
verdicts.fixes: (a) Standardise every layer's input by RMS (at least layer 1). Choose k_l by a function check on held-out old states, e.g. max clipped action change <= 0.005, then sim Pick >= 0.98, instead of worst-state eps. Report the private-size vs old-drift Pareto. (b) Ablate the merge with a 'no-merge' arm where the new skill runs on W0 plus its private part only. Post-hoc removal of 7-18% of an FT update dropped Stack to 0.29-0.68, so the merge is probably needed for exactness. (c) Store only Delta·R·U (out x k) per skill; the basis U is stored once per memory, about 11k params. CHEAPEST DECISIVE EXPERIMENT: about 20 GPU-min, no training. Run a post-hoc sim on the 6 existing FT checkpoints (units/full_s1, s2; pilot2/probe10_s1, s3; protect/monitor_s1, s2): Pick retention through the shared view with the old head, 1,024 episodes, at std-avg99, std eps = 1e-2, and raw-avg99 as a control that should reproduce about 0.86. A ready but UNTESTED script (no ManiSkill locally) is posthoc_split_sim.py in the directory below; copy it to haha-a, run it with PYTHONPATH=~/zhr_pve under scripts/with_gpu_mem.sh; it writes only to --out. GO if std-avg99 or eps = 1e-2 reaches >= 0.98 on all 6. Then run 4 seeds of LoRA r=8/16 on the frozen trunk (LR 3e-4 and 1e-3) to compare speed at equal retention. verdicts.method: ConflictSplit: full fine-tuning whose function-space conflict is routed to a private delta; everything else, even inside the old skills' space, stays shared
verdicts.verdict: NOT SUPPORTED AS A HEADLINE. Retention is plausible, but on this pair the conflict is not a few directions, so its private part is larger than OccSplit's at the same protection. Demote it to a diagnostic. Offline, I ran the one-shot version of its split: the function-null part of the full-FT update at theta_Pick on 512 anchors, then 10 step-halved Gauss-Newton restores. The old-skill view ends with held-out drift 0.003-0.008 and clipped arm change about 0.001 (FT: 9.8-17.9 and 0.084-0.128), so theta_sh should keep Pick. But the private delta is 68-70% of the FT update's norm, with rank (90% / 99% energy) of 15/25, 16/27-29 and 14/44-48 per layer, about the same as the FT update itself (6-7/17-19, 17-18/32-34, 18-20/56-66). Compressing it hurts the new skill. Gripper change on Stack states: r=8 (9% of the actor) 0.05-0.17; r=16 (17%) 0.056-0.13; r=32 (31%) 0.0004-0.0017. This Stack-side gripper change predicts sim Stack success well (Spearman -0.91), and post-hoc variants at 0.09-0.14 had Stack 0.29-0.68. So it needs about r=32 per layer (45k params, 31% of the actor) against OccSplit's 13-25%, which fails its own GO criterion of at most half OccSplit's size. The specified post-hoc procedure, GN restores starting from theta_FT with eta = 1, diverged on 2 of 4 checkpoints. With damping it converged, but the delta came out 1.26-2.0x the FT update with rank up to 118.
verdicts.closest_prior: Progress & Compress (Schwarz et al. 2018): an active column trains freely while a shared knowledge base absorbs it under EWC or distillation. PNN has the same free-trainer plus protected-shared structure. OGD and GEM supply the per-step function-null routing. TRGP and CUBER (Lin et al. 2022) keep task-specific private parts inside the old subspace. Model merging with per-task residuals (TALL-masks, Twin-Merging) stores the conflicting remainder.
verdicts.risks: (1) Private size: rank about 25-48 per layer. The online version accumulates the roughly 40% per-Adam-step conflict share seen in the BC replica, so its delta is unlikely to be smaller than the one-shot row part. (2) Compressing to r <= 16 without healing breaks the new skill. Healing (3 PPO iterations on B, C and the head) adds training and voids the 'bit-identical to FT' property. (3) A GN restore from large drift is unstable at eta = 1. (4) The claimed benefit of sharing the function-safe part with later skills (forward transfer) is untested and not obviously useful. (5) During training it doubles trunk memory and Jacobian work, and the shadow's first-order routing leaks second-order drift between restores. (6) The same retention-noise and proxy-calibration caveats as the other two apply.
verdicts.fixes: (a) Demote it from method to diagnostic or ablation. Report the conflict rank and the conflict map (phase histogram of the multipliers) as the analysis that motivates FN-PPO and OccSplit, and state plainly that the Pick->Stack conflict has rank 25-48 per layer. (b) If it is kept: split at theta_0 (one-shot or per step), never by GN from theta_FT; damp every restore; store the delta in OccSplit's basis (delta·U, out x k) rather than as SVD factors; choose r per layer by a Stack-side function check. CHEAPEST DECISIVE EXPERIMENT: about 20 GPU-min, post hoc, on the same 6 checkpoints. Measure sim Pick retention of theta_0 + null part + 10 damped restores (expect >= 0.98), and sim Stack success of theta_sh + rank-r(delta) at r = 16 and 32 (expect r=16 < 0.9 and r=32 about equal to FT). It is implemented in the same UNTESTED posthoc_split_sim.py. KILL the 'few directions' headline if Stack at r=16 is below 0.9. BASELINES: OccSplit at matched params, SVD-truncated FT delta, LoRA r=16/32, FT-N, PNN, FN-PPO (zero growth), FT, joint retraining. recommendation:
**Recommendation:** go with FN-PPO, with one change: its anchor states should come from the old skill's own closed-loop rollouts, not only from the stored bank. Rename it before submission because the name is too close to NSPO. The fallback is OccSplit, also renamed (e.g. "subspace copy-on-write"). ConflictSplit becomes a single sentence of diagnosis: its conflict has rank 25-48 per layer and is about 70% of the full fine-tuning (FT) update's norm, so it is not "a few directions".

**Why this method**
- **It matches the user's idea.** There is one network and every trunk parameter is shared. The only thing protected is what the old skills' actions depend on.
  - The function-null part of the FT update (about 70% of its norm²) barely moves Pick: drift 0.10-0.62.
  - The other 30% does all the damage: drift 9.6-17.5.
  - Protecting the input space keeps only 5-31% of the update, and GPM never reached 90%. That supports "the conflict is in the shared parameters, not the latent space" as a measured mechanism.
- **It has the best offline support.**
  - 99% of the old function's Gram trace lies in 130 directions, against 142,592 trunk parameters.
  - 512 anchors leave a 0.3-0.5% residual on held-out states.
  - In the BC replica, projecting gradient plus step learned the release as well as FT (conflict loss 1.60 vs 1.82) with 16 times less drift (0.21 vs 3.36). The Kronecker block projector did not protect (drift 3.16).
- **A result from 00:50 changes the design.**
  - block09g cut mean drift from 10 to 3.8, but Pick retention fell to 0.797. Every failure came after the grasp, and the error on the student's own states was 2.2 times the error on the teacher's states.
  - So protecting outputs on a stored bank is not enough in closed loop. The anchors have to follow the old skill's rollouts through the current network.
  - This is also the RL-specific novelty that OGD, GEM, SGP and NSPO lack.

## 1. Claim (one sentence)
When a skill is added to a robot policy by RL fine-tuning, the old skills are lost through a few hundred function-space directions: their own actions on their own closed-loop states. Projecting every PPO step out of exactly those directions, re-anchored each iteration by rolling the old skills through the current network, adds the skill to the same network within 1.25 times FT's steps, while every old skill keeps at least 0.98 success and the trunk gains no parameters.

The three hypotheses for the abstract:
- **H1, function locality:** the row-space part of the update does all the damage, and input-space protection throws away the useful part.
- **H2, closed-loop anchoring:** protection on a bank alone leaks through compounding errors.
- **H3, speed with zero growth:** at most 1.25 times FT's steps at 0.98 retention or better.

## 2. Algorithm (final form)

**Setup**
- The trunk θ is shared: three tanh Linear layers, 142,592 parameters.
- Each skill has a private head (8×256+8), a private log-std and a private critic.
- The new skill's head starts as a copy of the source head. All earlier heads are frozen.
- A snapshot θ0 taken at the start of the new skill gives the teacher targets μ_j*(x). In a chain, retention is still reported against the original experts.

**Each PPO iteration**
1. **Anchors.** Take 512 states per old skill from a closed-loop pool.
   - The pool holds deterministic rollouts of old skill j in its own task, through the current trunk and head j.
     - ManiSkill: a side process runs 256 envs × 50 steps every 5 iterations. The pool is the iteration-0 rollout plus the last two refreshes.
     - a2r: a 64-env slice of the training env, excluded from PPO.
   - At least 50% of anchors are after the grasp, and at least 20% are within 2.5 cm of the goal.
   - Labels are μ_j* computed at θ0 (DAgger labels). Sampling uses a separate generator.
2. **Gram matrix.** At the current θ, take the layer inputs Z_l and the σ-scaled backprop vectors G_l for 4,096 rows per old skill.
   - K = Σ_l (G_l G_lᵀ) ⊙ (Z_l Z_lᵀ + 1) + δI, with δ = 1e-4·tr K / M, in fp64, factored by Cholesky.
   - In chains, keep the directions holding 99.99% of the trace.
3. **Every Adam step.**
   - Project the trunk gradient: α = K⁻¹Jg, then g_l −= G_lᵀ diag(α) Z_l (and G_lᵀα for the bias).
   - Take the Adam step, then project the realised trunk step again with the same K.
   - Heads, log-std and critic are not projected. Log ρ_g and ρ_s, the shares of gradient and step that are removed.
4. **Damped Gauss-Newton restore** on 512 fresh closed-loop anchors.
   - The new head's means on 256 states of the current batch are added as equality rows, so the new skill stays fixed.
   - Compute β = K_aug⁻¹ [e; 0] and set θ += η J_augᵀ β.
   - Start with η = 1 and halve it until drift on 2,048 held-out closed-loop states falls and the new policy's KL on the batch is at most 0.01. If neither holds, skip the restore.
5. **Exploration.** Apply a std floor of 1.0 on the new skill's gripper (or new action dimension) only if the source's deterministic success on the new task is below 10% in a 256-episode probe. The floor is global, with no seam gating.

**Logs**
- Drift on bank states and on closed-loop states.
- Restore acceptance rate and the KL it induces.
- Conflict map: phase histogram of the top 5% of |α|.
- Online old-skill success, reported by the side process.

**Code**
- An "fn" mode in the existing `Protector` in `wrwl/ppo.py`, reusing its `project_grad`/`project` hooks (about 150 lines).
- A side worker built on `retention_eval.py` (about 60 lines).
- The restore (about 40 lines).
- The linear algebra costs well under 0.1 s per iteration.

Pre-register before launch. Launch Nov 2, decide Nov 4.

**Protocol**

- One change: no early stop. Every run goes to 3M steps, so retention is read at t90 and again after continued training.
- Seeds 1-4.

**New arms (32 runs)**

| Arm | What it tests |
|---|---|
| FT | Reference. GPU runs are bit-reproducible, so seed 1's prefix must match the old train.csv exactly (built-in bit-check). |
| FN-CL | The method. |
| FN-bank | Anchors from `data/bc_pick_c1.pt` only; tests H2. |

| Restore-CL | FT plus step 4 every iteration, no per-step projection: is the projection needed? |
| KL-CL at λ* and 3λ* | Soft penalty on the same closed-loop anchors: hard vs soft protection on the same states. λ* is the largest coefficient from the queued bank-distill sweep with t90 ≤ 1.9M; use {1, 3} if the sweep is unfinished. |
| Head-only at LR 1e-3 | Can this pair separate methods at all? |

Reused with no new runs: head-only at 3e-4 (3.1M / 0.992), 5% and 20% units, block09/095/099 and their gradient-projected versions, gpm095g, distill 0.01/0.1/1 on the bank, and EWC/L2 from the haha-a queue.

**Metrics**
- t90: the first of 3 consecutive evals at 0.9 or above.
- Retention R: Pick deterministic success through the Pick head and the current trunk, 1,024 episodes, at t90 and at 3M. Also an online curve of 256 episodes every 5 iterations.
- After-grasp error on teacher states vs student states (`forgetting_closedloop.py`).
- ρ, drift, restore acceptance and the conflict map.
- Parameters added per skill: 2,064 in the actor.

**Decision rule**
- **Separability first.** If head-only at 1e-3 has median t90 ≤ 1.9M, rerun FT, KL-CL and FN-CL on Pick→PlaceCube before making any claim.
- **GO (FN-CL is the headline)** if all of these hold:
  - median t90 ≤ 1.9M and no seed above 2.5M;
  - mean R ≥ 0.98 at t90 and ≥ 0.97 at 3M, with no seed below 0.95;
  - FN-CL beats both KL-CL arms on the speed-retention frontier.
- **What shapes the claim:**
  - If FN-bank is at least 3 points below FN-CL, or has any seed below 0.95, H2 stands. Otherwise drop the side process.
  - If Restore-CL is within 1 point and 0.2M of FN-CL, lead with the simpler restore.
  - If the no-restore arm matches FN-CL, drop the restore.
- **Zero-growth Pareto point only:** R ≥ 0.98 but t90 between 1.9M and 2.2M. Continue, and start the fallback in parallel.
- **KILL, go to the fallback:** median t90 above 2.2M (no better than 5% units, which need no Jacobians), or mean R below 0.97.

## 5. Main risk and its early warning

**Main risk: speed.** At initialisation, 99.6% of the new skill's trunk gradient lies in the old skill's row space. This is because the head is a copy and the conflict sits on Pick's densest states. FN-CL could then run at head-only speed (3.1M) and lose to 5% units (2.2M, no Jacobians).
- **Warning sign, about 10 min into each run:** at 1.0M steps, ρ_g is still above 0.95, and FN-CL's eval success is below the midpoint of head-only's and FT's in at least 3 of 4 seeds.
- **Response:** one pre-registered rescue, `--fn_warmup 5` plus a private-head LR of 1e-3, 4 seeds, under 1 GPU-h. If FN-CL still tracks head-only, KILL and switch to the fallback the same day.

**Second risk: closed-loop leak even with exact rows.** Warning sign: online retention below 0.95 before t90, or after-grasp error on student states more than twice the error on teacher states. That was block09g's pattern.

**Third risk: a2r R0 below 5 points,** known Nov 3-4.

## 6. Fallback (trigger: KILL on Nov 4, or failure at D3)
OccSplit, renamed. Train by plain FT with the floor, so speed equals FT by construction. Then split the update per layer, with RMS-standardised inputs:
- Choose k_l by a function check: the maximum clipped old-action change must be ≤ 0.005 on held-out bank and closed-loop states.
- Keep ΔW·R·U_l private, stored factored (out × k_l).
- Merge ΔW·R(I−UUᵀ)R⁻¹ into the shared trunk.

**Claim:** the new skill is exact at FT speed and old skills stay within ε, for 13-25% of the actor per skill. Step 0 runs Nov 1. It is a GO if the 99%-energy subspace (standardised inputs) or ε = 1e-2 keeps Pick ≥ 0.98 on all 6 FT checkpoints. Whatever FN-CL achieves becomes the zero-growth end of a single Pareto plot: no private part → the occupied part → a full copy (FT-N). It needs no new a2r runs: the F-plain runs are split after training.
